### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `381b7f25131f2376ea7d1ff57575f06026b8f3e7` — the merge of head `49b7049edb9149a0bec96768e320ad9b86ed3db8` into base `9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 381b7f25131f2376ea7d1ff57575f06026b8f3e7 && git checkout 381b7f25131f2376ea7d1ff57575f06026b8f3e7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac 49b7049edb9149a0bec96768e320ad9b86ed3db8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac && git merge --no-ff 49b7049edb9149a0bec96768e320ad9b86ed3db8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9edd6e783b48ad5e326060e4c4c35040f159deac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `49b7049edb9149a0bec96768e320ad9b86ed3db8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/url-boundary.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-url-credentials.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.ts + .changeset/url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.md, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (the entry refinement and `connectorUrlCredentialRefusal`), packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts (the mongo `credentialsRef` arm), packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts (`buildMongoAuth`, the username injection), packages/spec/src/data/driver/pg-url-grammar.server.ts, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.md (the `integration/` and `datasource.zod.ts` rows), PR #29573's body (the ruling text it quotes), and the five spec test files and two dogfood files of the diff, read for what they pin

Inputs: the PR body as rewritten for this round, the file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge-base `9edd6e783b`, the check-runs on this head, ruling D verbatim, and the earlier independent review's two "within the ruling" findings. The tree was judged, not the body's account of it.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set changes, per door and half, read off the tree.**

- *Datasource, userinfo half* (`credentialFreeUrl` → `urlUserinfoPassword` → `urlUserinfoSpan`): the password is read on the cleaned string — both ends trimmed of U+0000–U+0020, every ASCII tab, LF and CR deleted anywhere — at RFC 3986's authority and last-`@` boundaries. Narrowing: a URL whose non-empty password is reachable only after that cleaning is now refused; on `main` the anchored regex missed it. Unchanged: a bare username, an empty password, and any string with no `//`.
- *Datasource, query half* (`urlCredentialQueryParams` → `credentialQueryParamOf`): each raw pair has tab, LF and CR deleted before the `=` split and the decoded, case-folded name match. This half applies no end-trim (the ruling names trimming for the userinfo half only). The one divergence from the parser's reading: a last pair whose value is non-empty only by characters the parser trims at the string's end is refused here where the parser reads no credential. Over-refusal in the safe direction, no exposure.
- *Connector, userinfo half* (`connectorUrlWithoutUserinfo`): the same `urlUserinfoSpan`, so two narrowings against `main`: the cleaning, and an authority that starts at a scheme-relative `//`. Still the whole userinfo (#29573's posture), on every string under `providerConfig` and `auth` outside the four withheld maps.
- *Connector, query half*: the `URL_SCHEME_RE` gate is gone; `urlCredentialQueryParams` runs on every walked string. Narrowing: a non-URL string holding a credential-named pair with a value is refused.

**Read/write symmetry ("refused ⇔ rewritten").**

- *Connector*: the write refuses iff `connectorUrlWithoutUserinfo(value) !== value` or a pair matches; the read rewrites with the same two functions on the same string. Identical predicate, exact.
- *Datasource, userinfo*: the read removes `[colon, @)` at the raw offsets; the write refuses iff the cleaned password is non-empty. "Rewritten ⇒ refused" fails in exactly one case, pre-existing on `main` and flagged by the dev: an empty password (`user:@host`) is rewritten to `user@host` while the write accepts it. Credential-neutral; the served form passes the write door, and `service-datasource`'s restore compares against `redactUrlCredentials(stored)`, so a save of the served form keeps the stored value. Not a defect of this PR. The prose on `redactUrlCredentialQueryParams` saying `redactUrlPassword` "also leaves" that form is wrong on `main` and still wrong here (no pin asserts it either way) — prose, should-fix.
- *Query, both doors*: write and read filter the same raw pairs through the same `credentialQueryParamOf`. The userinfo always precedes the first `?` (the authority is anchored at the string's cleaned start and ends before any `?`), so the read's order — userinfo first, then pairs — cannot change the pair set.
- *Offset mapping*: `rawOffsets[i]` is the authored index of cleaned character i, with one sentinel at `text.length`; `start`, `end` (the `@`) and `colon` are all taken through it, so a deletion in the scheme, between `//` and the username, inside the username or inside the password shifts nothing. Walked by hand on each of those, on an empty userinfo (`start === end`, only the `@` goes), on a userinfo ending the string, and on a multi-`@` password. The sentinel is never indexed on a reachable path. No off-by-one found; the served form passes the write door in every case walked.

**Accessor semantics.** `urlUserinfoUsername` and `urlUserinfoPassword` now answer the cleaned component (percent-encoding still preserved). Consumers at this head: `credentialFreeUrl` (presence only); the `datasource.zod.ts` mongo `credentialsRef` arm (presence — it now agrees with the client on a URL behind surrounding whitespace, where `main` refused "names no user"); and `buildMongoAuth`, which injects as `auth.username` the username the mongodb client itself reads from the same URL after its own WHATWG cleaning — an alignment, not a drift. The "RAW component" sentence on `urlUserinfoUsername` now means percent-encoding only; `urlUserinfo`'s note states the cleaning. Prose, not blocking.

**Check-runs on `49b7049edb`.** 0 failed; every gate that ran is green, 9 skipped by their own conditions. The `mergeable_state: unstable` reading is accounted for by `Check Changeset` (workflow `PR Automation`): run 41618651092 success at 10:24Z on this head; after the body rewrite two further `pull_request` runs on this same head started at 11:29–11:30Z — 41627905511 cancelled (superseded by its successor) and 41628005836, in progress when the review began and completed success at 11:32Z. Both belong to this PR; the only non-green conclusion on the head is that superseded cancellation, and the gate's newest reading is green. The `vercel`, `fly-io`, `cloudflare-workers-and-pages`, `claude` and `objectstack-fleet` suites show `queued` with no runs — third-party app suites, not gates of this repo.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` **minor** with **BREAKING**: right for a declared accept-set narrowing under ADR-0087. The changeset carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the registration marker and a FROM → TO that the tree refuses and accepts as written.
- D3 entry `18.url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.ts`: `surface` names both doors and every entry door; `reason` states all four narrowings (trim, tab/newline deletion, one userinfo grammar, any connector string), the bare-username carve-out and the deliberate absence of a mechanical rewrite; `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are actionable. Each sentence was checked against the code; the amended wording matches the tree. The `18.` prefix is the series prefix the other entries use.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is correct: both save doors accept less; the carry-forward contract is unchanged (datasource restore mirrors the one composite `redactUrlCredentials`; the connector re-grafts by `redactedKeys` and the withheld maps are untouched).
- No public export added or removed: `url-boundary.ts` and `connector-url-credentials.ts` are internal; the removed `URL_SCHEME_RE` / `URL_USERINFO_RE` had no consumer on `main` outside the connector redactor (the `view.zod.ts` constant of the same name is its own). The strictness ledger's `integration/` and `datasource.zod.ts` rows describe shapes this PR does not touch; no row changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tab/LF/CR deleted anywhere before judging** — within ruling D's purpose. The tree's own `pg-url-grammar.server.ts` records that `pg-connection-string` parses through `new URL(str, base)`, i.e. a WHATWG parse, and the mysql2 and mongodb notes in `common.zod.ts` point the same way; a password the parser reads only after deletion was accepted on `main`. Note also that the pg grammar arm already refuses a leading *space* for postgres (its space re-encoding makes the value relative) but not a leading tab, LF, CR or other C0 character, and that arm is server-only — so this value-level rule is the only guard in the browser build. Accept.
- **One scheme-optional userinfo grammar at the connector** — the weaker leg, as the body declares. Cost on the tree: any string under `providerConfig` or `auth` whose cleaned form starts with `//` and holds an `@` before any `/`, `?` or `#` is refused as a userinfo; prose or an argument-list element can take that shape. Benefit: a scheme-relative reference is read with its userinfo by every consumer that resolves it. The refusal is located and names the fix; the body's in-repo scan found 0 hits. Within the ruling; it stays the veto window the body puts to the maintainer. Not blocking. Should-fix candidate, the maintainer's call: on the scheme-relative arm only, require the host part to hold no whitespace, which a URL parser rejects as a host — the purpose "the check sees what the parser sees" would then hold on both sides of that arm.
- **Open question, escalated: special-scheme strings.** A string with a special scheme (`http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss`, `ftp`, `file`) whose authority is not introduced by `//` is judged by neither door at this head — the shared grammar requires `//` — so such a value is stored and served; no built-in provider sends it (they fetch, and fetch refuses a userinfo). Leaving it out of this PR is right: it would be a third reading of the grammar, outside ruling D's "one grammar at both doors" text, and no datasource driver uses a special scheme, so it would in effect be connector-only. Symmetry holds there (neither refused nor rewritten); it is an accept-set question, not an asymmetry, and not a FAIL. It needs a maintainer ruling on whether the shared authority grammar admits a special scheme's slash-tolerant forms at both doors.
- **libsql.** The body's claim that `@libsql/core` applies no cleaning cannot be verified from this tree (no installed client to read; nothing was run). It is not load-bearing for the verdict: the tree's own measured note is that libsql reads `?authToken=` by the exact decoded key and refuses a userinfo, so no value libsql opens is refused by this PR (see ④).

### ④ Design judgment

- **Off-by-one on deletions before the colon or the `@`:** none; see the offset walk in ①.
- **A pair whose name collides with a credential name only after cleaning:** the write refuses it and the read removes the raw pair whole; both go through `credentialQueryParamOf`, and the parser's `URLSearchParams` reads the same name. Consistent.
- **Percent-encoded tab (`%09`):** neither the parser nor this code deletes it (deletion precedes percent-decoding on both sides); the decoded name then differs from the credential name on both sides. Consistent; nothing to fix.
- **A value valid for libsql but now refused:** a turso URL behind surrounding whitespace, or with a tab, LF or CR in its scheme, holding a userinfo was accepted on `main` and is refused now; libsql opens neither (its scheme must start the string, and the turso contract has refused a userinfo since #8082). A `?authToken=` name that matches only after deleting such a character is refused now and was never read by libsql, which matches the exact decoded key. No working value lost.
- **Performance of cleaning every string under `providerConfig`:** `urlAsParsed` builds a character-by-character copy plus a per-character offset array for every walked string — an inline OpenAPI document's strings included — on every entry parse and every served read, the clean common case included; `main`'s scheme gate skipped most strings. Bounded by metadata size, not on a request path; acceptable. Should-fix, non-blocking: a fast path when the string needs no cleaning (identity offsets), or a `//`-presence check before building the map.
- **Tests:** names state the rule; refusals name parts and position, never the value; every placeholder is fake. Pinned: refused ⇔ rewritten at both doors, the mapped offsets, CONTROLs for a bare username, an empty credential value, a tab in an ordinary name, a scheme-relative authority without userinfo, an `@` in a scheme-relative path; both HTTP save doors in dogfood with nothing stored on refusal and the stored row never rewritten.
- **Must-fix:** none.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-i`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
